title: Ashtpadi 19, salok: nothing goes along
hookLine: nothing goes with you except devotion (Sukhmani 19)

lines: A LIFETIME OF THINGS, ALL LEFT.
THE PERSON ISN'T IN ANY OF IT.
cards: Anyone who has cleared out a parent's home knows the feeling. The drawers of rubber bands. The good china used twice.
The boxes of papers that once mattered terribly: tax forms, warranties, letters. A lifetime of things, and every last bit of it stayed behind.
You stand in the half-empty room holding a coffee mug and realize the person isn't in any of it. The salok of the nineteenth ashtpadi says this out loud, and then says what isn't left behind.

teach.h: SAATH NA CHAALAI: DOES NOT GO ALONG.
teach.b: The salok, in paraphrase: nothing goes along with you except devotion; all the poison of worldly things is ash. Earn the Name of the Lord; Nanak, this is the excellent wealth. Three words open it.
Saath: with, alongside. Na chaalai: does not go. Bin bhajan: except devotion, the singing and remembering of God.
So the first line is a short inventory: everything you own, and next to almost every item, does not go.
Then the strong image: bikhiaa saglee chhaar. Bikhiaa is a word Gurbani uses for maya's poison, the pull of worldly things. Chhaar is ash.
Not evil, exactly. Ash: what's left when the fire has burned out. The house, the car, the savings account aren't wicked.
They're ash-in-waiting. Then the turn, and it's a money word.
Kamaavanaa: to earn. Earn the Name. The salok doesn't tell you to stop earning; Sikhs are expected to work honestly and provide for their families.
It tells you what else to earn, and it calls the Name dhan, wealth, and saar, the excellent, the essential. So this isn't a hymn against wealth.
It's a hymn about which wealth travels.
Over the next days the ashtpadi looks at what stays behind and what goes along. Today, only the inventory. And the salok makes no threat.
It points at the room full of things and says: none of this comes with you, except the devotion.

how: Sikhs reciting Sukhmani Sahib open the nineteenth ashtpadi with the salok saath na chaalai bin bhajan, and Sikh life pairs honest earning with remembering the Name as the wealth that lasts.

o: the savings you leave to your family
with, alongside: what goes along with you
a long road walked on pilgrimage

games.q: the salok of ashtpadi 19 — tap the pairs.

s: the salok tells Sikhs to stop earning money
it says what else to earn: the Name, the excellent wealth.
the salok calls the Name a kind of wealth
dhan saar: the excellent, essential wealth.
the salok calls worldly things wicked
it calls them ash: what remains when the fire has burned out.

games.q: you're clearing out a loved one's home after they've died. what does the nineteenth salok say went along with them?
games.why: saath na chaalai bin bhajan: nothing goes along except devotion. the things are ash; the Name is the wealth that travels.

practice: Let your eyes move slowly around the room, the furniture, the phone, the clothes, the books, and to each thing say silently, without sadness, just accurately: this stays.
Then close your eyes and ask what, if anything, is going along with you, and let the question sit unanswered.

wordCard.voice: Saath, with or alongside: its salok says saath na chaalai bin bhajan, nothing goes along except devotion; earn the Name, the excellent wealth.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: saath, with, alongside, as in saath na chaalai, does not go along.

carryVoice: Your line: nothing goes along. The things are ash-in-waiting; the Name is the wealth that travels. That's day five hundred ten.
